feedback: 1) Format is mostly correct (states declared, FINAL_STATES present with an accepting state u3), but the else self-loops are incomplete: u2 and u3 must also cover all propositions they don't name, including regressions. 2) `door_open` is non-monotone: it can turn false again by toggle and is never relocked, yet u2 ignores it — in u2 the door can close while the agent is in the right room, but that doesn't affect reachability since the agent is already past the door; this is acceptable only if the else self-loop in u2 also handles door_open false. It does via `(u2, else) -> u2`, so semantics are fine there. 3) In u1, the else self-loop must cover `key_lost` co-occurring with other propositions; per constraints key_lost never co-occurs with has_door_key/door_open/target_picked_up, so it's fine. 4) However, there is a semantic gap: after picking up the key (u1), the agent could drop the key while door_open is false — that is key_lost, correctly handled. But after door_open, if the agent re-enters u2 and the door is still open, the drop of the key is not key_lost — handled, since u2 ignores key_lost. 5) Missing coverage: the task says never drop the key while the door is closed; but u0→u1 only requires has_door_key. If the agent never gets the key and goes straight — impossible per constraints, fine. 6) Real problem: once in u2, the agent could be without the key and the door could toggle shut again — but relock is impossible per constraints ('never relocked'), fine. 7) Reward safety: no progress reward on ufail-adjacent regressions; rewards are sparse/bounded, acceptable, though paper format typically wants dense-but-bounded shaping — this sparse form is acceptable. 8) Ordered transition coverage: the machine never returns from ufail and never handles reaching u3 via any path other than target_picked_up — correct. The main defect: in state u1, if the agent toggles the door open, that moves to u2; but if in u0 the agent somehow triggers door_open — impossible without key, fine. Remaining issue: state ufail is not accepting/terminal-declared but that is allowed as a sink. Overall the machine looks largely correct; the one clear defect is that `(u0, else) -> u0` and `(u1, else) -> u1` etc. don't explicitly list regressions of door_open from u2 (door_open false) — the else loop covers it, so no fix strictly needed. Verdict: the structure covers the task; key_lost in u1 correctly encodes 'never drop the key while the door is closed' as a failure sink with penalty. Accept after confirming else loops cover all unlisted propositions in every state, which they do. However, FINAL_STATES lists only u3 and ufail is a trap — acceptable. One genuine concern: the transition (u1, key_lost) → ufail fires even if the agent later recovers the key; that is intentional per task. Accepting with minor notes.
